about: The dialogue font's text encoding: what each byte of a string drawn through DrawString and the message window does, and which character each cell of the font sheet draws (the HUD font's strings, the monsters', bosses' and spells' names, have their own encoding: text/hud_font.json). One definition for every tool: tools/text_codec.py reads it (the dialogue bank's extraction and build, and the project's ROM map, a research tool outside this repository). Written from the matched C and the original ROM.

font.metrics: gFontMetrics[0] = {width 10, height 13, advance 10, lineHeight 14}: the one font; DrawString draws cell c of a strip from s = width * c

codes.evidence: DrawString draws a byte below 0x7F as that cell of the current row (30 cells use 300 of a strip's 304 texels)
DrawString moves the pen by the advance and draws nothing

codes.source text: placed by the rule, or {row N}
codes.evidence: DrawString loads strip N of gFontSheet; at a page turn the message window keeps the last row, palette and font codes for the next page (DrawDialogueBox)
DrawString loads palette N of gTextPalettes (the ROM holds palettes 0-3)
DrawString sets gFont to N; gFontMetrics holds one font (entry 0)
DrawString sets gFontSpacing to the index itself (16-31), added to every advance
DrawString starts a new line (lineHeight); PageMessage ends a row
DrawDialogueBox: the typing delay becomes D_80061660[byte & 7] times the message speed
DrawDialogueBox waits for A or B once a glyph is on the page; PageMessage ends the page
DrawDialogueBox resizes the window (SetMessageWindowSize) and sets the save prompt's flags

codes.source text: the end of a string's body
codes.evidence: every reader of a string stops at it
no case in DrawString; the message window counts it as a pause

row select rule: a glyph is preceded by a row select when no glyph came directly before it in the string, or when the glyph before it is in another row; a select the rule would not write is stated as {row N}. Every string of the original's dialogue bank follows the rule.

npc_names.about: An NPC file's name pool: the speaker names NPC records point at (StartNPCText copies one into gSpeakerName).
npc_names.limits: A name may be at most 0x20 bytes, its 0xFF included (StartNPCText copies 0x20; a longer one would lose its end mark).
npc_names.references: NpcRecord.name, a pointer (u8*) into the pool of the file its area loads (gNpcBlobs) or of Shannon's block
npc_names.layout: each string on a 4-byte step from the pool's start, zero fill between, the pool padded to 16 with zeros: the original's layout (the code copies a name byte by byte and needs neither)

parts.name: npc
parts.label: gDialogueNpc
parts.about: The dialogue bank's NPC strings: what an NPC says (StartNPCText, StartNPCTalk).
parts.limits: A string may be at most 0x4B0 bytes, MESSAGE_TEXT_SIZE in the C (StartNPCText reads that many; tools/text_build.py stops if the two differ).
parts.references: NpcRecord.message and .altMessage, u16 offsets from the base (StartNPCText DMAs 0x4B0 bytes from base + offset; StartNPCTalk reads altMessage for talk types 2 and 5)

parts.name: signs
parts.label: gDialogueSigns
parts.about: The dialogue bank's sign strings: a sign's, door's or shelf's name and text (LoadSignText).
parts.limits: A name (marked name) may be at most 0x20 bytes, a text 0x200 (LoadSignText reads them so).
parts.references: SignObject's name and text offsets (+0x1C, +0x1E), u16 from the base (LoadSignText DMAs 0x20 and 0x200 bytes)

grades.verified: a source's character, checked against the cell's bitmap in the original ROM's font sheet
grades.corrected: the bitmap and the strings that use the cell name another character than the leads
grades.uncertain: no character is established: the source text writes the cell as {R,C}; the lead is kept
grades.duplicate: the bitmap draws the character of another cell ("same as"): one character encodes to one cell, so the source text writes this cell as {R,C}; the lead is kept
grades.empty: no texel set: the cell draws nothing

verification: Every cell a lead names was checked against its own bitmap in the original Japanese ROM's font sheet (all 30 rows rendered); where a bitmap and a lead disagreed, the strings that use the cell decided. 832 cells verified, 1 corrected (12,15), 1 a second drawing of another cell's character (22,22), 1 left uncertain (18,5), 65 empty. Each cell keeps its source and, where they differ, its lead.

sources.name: eltale-font-tool
sources.about: Iconoclast's Eltale Monsters Translator (2024; its source states the GPL-3.0-or-later): its glyph table (font.c's fontmap) named 484 cells. Used as leads: only the cell-to-character facts, each checked against the cell's bitmap in the original ROM; none of its code or other material is used.

sources.name: QuestEdit
sources.about: a Quest 64 editor (its author is unknown; no licence was found): its text table named the 351 kanji the first left unknown. Used as leads, the same way: only the cell-to-character facts, each checked against the cell's bitmap in the original ROM.
